title: Population, long run (modelled)
note: Modelled by the HYDE 3.2 history database from historical and archaeological population estimates, spread over the land by models; before about 1800 these are estimates with wide uncertainty (not shown by the source), and early millennia rest on very few figures.

title: Population at each census

title: Population
note: Census years to 1961 (the area of the six counties before 1921), annual estimates from 1971.

title: Population at each census
note: The Great Famine of 1845–52 and emigration: 6.53 million in 1841, 5.11 million in 1851, falling until 1961.

title: Towns and cities of 10,000 people or more
note: Counted from Buringh's city database at each date (one value per century to 1500, then every 50 years). Only places that later became sizeable cities are in the database, so early counts are a lower bound; many early populations are the author's estimates.

title: Share of people living in towns
note: UN estimates by each country's own definition of urban; no comparable open series before 1950.

title: Share of people living in towns
note: UN estimates by each country's own definition of urban.

title: Homes (dwelling stock)
note: Census counts of dwellings to 1961, then annual estimates; definitions changed between censuses.

title: Life expectancy at birth
note: Period life expectancy, pulled down by deaths in infancy. Before 1841 the values are reconstructions for England (Zijdeman et al. / Clio Infra) at irregular dates. Dips: 1918 influenza, 2020 COVID-19.

title: Income per head (GDP per person)
region: England to 1700, Great Britain to 1870, then UK
note: In 2011 international dollars (adjusted for prices). The Maddison Project uses Broadberry et al. (2015) for England before 1870; a single point for AD 1000.

title: Income per head (GDP per person)
note: 1820, 1870, 1913, then yearly from 1921. Recent values are inflated by multinational companies' accounts.

title: Tree cover from pollen
note: Tree cover reconstructed from pollen in lake and bog cores (the REVEALS model), averaged over 1° cells with an estimate; one value per time window (500 years before 1000 BC, shorter later). The band is ±1 standard error; which cells have data changes between windows.

title: CO₂ from coal, oil and gas
note: Fossil fuels and cement, from the Global Carbon Budget.

title: CO₂ from coal, oil and gas
Sulphur dioxide emitted
note: Mostly from burning coal: the smoke and acid rain of the industrial age, cut by the Clean Air Acts (1956, 1968) and the move from coal.

title: Temperature, yearly average
note: The longest instrumental temperature record in the world. 1659–1722 values are rounded and rest on few sources.

title: Rainfall, yearly total
note: Rescued and homogenised long series; early decades rest on few stations.

title: Summer temperature from tree rings
note: July–August temperature from Scots pine ring density, as a difference from the 1961–90 average; band ±2 standard errors.

title: Summer temperature, reconstructed
note: June–August temperature from tree rings and documents, as a difference from the 1961–90 average; band ±2σ.

title: Temperature since the Ice Age
note: From pollen, marine and lake records worldwide (median of five methods), as a difference from 1800–1900, in 100-year steps; band 5–95%. A latitude band, not the isles themselves.

title: Carbon dioxide in the air
note: Ice-core air bubbles from Antarctica (well mixed worldwide), then measured in the open air. Joined from the sources named, each over its own years.

title: Methane in the air
note: Ice-core air bubbles from Antarctica (well mixed worldwide), then measured in the open air. Joined from the sources named, each over its own years.

title: Nitrous oxide in the air
note: Ice-core air bubbles from Antarctica (well mixed worldwide), then measured in the open air. Joined from the sources named, each over its own years.

title: Volcanic eruptions (sulphur into the stratosphere)
note: Each point is one eruption found in Greenland and Antarctic ice; big ones cooled the isles' summers for a year or two (536, 540, 1257, 1783 Laki, 1815 Tambora).

title: The sun's output
note: From beryllium-10 and carbon-14 in ice and tree rings, 22-year averages, as a difference from the 1986 solar minimum. Low phases include the Spörer (c. 1450) and Maunder (c. 1680) minima.

title: Sea level
note: Yearly mean sea level at the tide gauge, as a difference from its 1961–80 average. Relative to the land, which is still rising in Scotland and sinking in the south after the Ice Age.
